sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Bay County?
sections.html:
Three layers touch a Bay County tax bill: the local assessor, the township or city treasurer, and the county treasurer. The county describes itself as 14 townships and 4 cities with about 102,000 residents, and it notes that most assessing and tax work in Michigan sits with those local units rather than the county.

The county Equalization Department checks that local assessments line up. Its duties page says it runs sales and appraisal studies by class in each local unit so assessments are held at 49 to 50 percent across the county, and it prepares the Millage Reduction Report. It does not set the value of your individual parcel. The local assessor does.

  • Local assessor: sets your assessed value and mails change notices. Every Bay County township and city has an assessor on the county's published list.
  • Township or city treasurer: sends the July and December bills and takes payment first.
  • Bay County Treasurer: collects delinquent real property tax, certifies deeds for tax status, and chairs the county Land Bank Authority.
  • Equalization Department: parcel ownership, land descriptions and assessment records. It keeps descriptions for most of the county, except Bangor and Hampton Townships and the cities of Bay City and Essexville, which maintain their own.

sections.h2: When are Bay County property taxes billed and where do I pay?
sections.html:
Real property tax is billed twice a year by the township or city treasurer, in July and December. Anything still unpaid to that local treasurer on February 28 moves to the County Treasurer for collection under MCL 211.78.

The County Treasurer works from the Bay County Building at 515 Center Ave. in Bay City, on the sixth floor, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The office phone is 989-895-4285. Payments of delinquent tax can go several ways, summarized below.

Ways to pay the Bay County Treasurer. Source: Bay County Treasurer payment options page.
MethodWhat the county says
MailCheck, card or ACH. Must arrive by the last business day of the month, or be postmarked on the last day, to get that month's payoff figure.
OnlineCredit card with a 3% fee.
In personCheck, cash, Visa, Mastercard or Discover, plus ACH forms.
PhoneCard payments with a 3% fee. Wire instructions on request.
Drop boxRear entrance of the building, reached from 5th Street.
Automatic ACHOne time, weekly or every other week on Fridays, or monthly on the 10th and/or 20th.

Never email card or bank details. The county asks that sensitive forms be mailed, faxed or phoned in.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Bay County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the local board of review, which Michigan law sets to meet on the second Monday in March (MCL 211.30). A city or township may move the first session to the Tuesday or Wednesday after. The board must sit at least 12 hours that week, and at least three of the hours must run after 6 p.m.

The board has to notify each person who protested, in writing, by the first Monday in June. That notice must explain the right to go on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. For homes, the tribunal petition deadline is July 31 of the tax year, and for commercial and industrial property it is May 31 (MCL 205.735a). Residential owners generally have to protest at the board of review first.

  • Call the assessor for your township or city to ask how that unit takes protests, including whether it accepts letters.
  • Get the appraisal record card from the township or city. The county Equalization office says those cards come from the local unit.
  • Equalization answers questions about parcel ownership, descriptions and tax information, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

A dispute over a principal residence exemption goes to the July or December board of review before the tribunal can hear it.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Bay County homeowners?
sections.html:
The Equalization page for Bay County describes the disabled veteran exemption. A veteran qualifies by meeting any one of three tests: a federal finding of permanent and total disability from service at the 100 percent rate, a certificate for specially adapted housing assistance, or a rating of individually unemployable.

The unremarried surviving spouse can keep the exemption, provided the spouse is a Michigan resident. Owners must apply every year, between tax day and the final adjournment of the local board of review, by filing an affidavit and the federal paperwork with the local assessor.

For help with a bill you cannot pay, ask the County Treasurer's office directly about options before the February 28 transfer date. The county also runs a Land Bank Authority, created by the Board of Commissioners on August 11, 2009, which handles unusual property problems and properties that may not sell at a public auction.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax when I sell a Bay County house?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the parcel, so it has to be dealt with before or at the sale. For a deed that carries a warranty covenant, a land contract, or a condominium master deed, the register of deeds needs a tax certificate under MCL 211.135 showing taxes paid for the five years before the instrument. In Bay County that certificate costs $5 and is paid by a separate check to the County Treasurer.

A quitclaim deed with no covenant of warranty falls outside that rule, but a buyer's lender or title company usually wants the tax picture cleared anyway. Ask the closing agent to pull the payoff from the treasurer before the closing date.

On delinquent parcels, the county treasurer acts as the foreclosing governmental unit. Under MCL 211.78 a forfeited parcel can lead to a foreclosure judgment if it is not redeemed, so a seller with back taxes should call the treasurer early rather than wait for a notice.

The deed also triggers transfer tax. The Register of Deeds posts $7.50 per thousand dollars of price for the state and $1.10 per thousand for the county. On a house sold at the county's Census median of $152,200, that works out to roughly $1,141 state plus $167 county, or about $1,309 total.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Bay County homes?
sections.html:
The latest QuickFacts estimate puts Bay County at 102,123 people on 442 square miles of land, down 1.7 percent from the April 2020 base. There are 48,704 housing units and 45,103 households, and 77.0 percent of homes are owner occupied.

The median value of an owner occupied home for 2020 to 2024 is $152,200, and median household income is $61,763. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,249, while owners without one report $557. About 24.2 percent of residents are 65 or older, which matters for sellers weighing exemptions and downsizing.

faqs.q: When do Bay County property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: Taxes not paid to the township or city treasurer by February 28 move to the Bay County Treasurer for collection under MCL 211.78. Call 989-895-4285 for a payoff figure.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Bay County tax bill online?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Treasurer takes credit cards online for a 3% fee. Checks, cash, mail, phone, wire, a drop box and automatic ACH debits are also listed on the county's payment page.

faqs.q: Who sets my Bay County assessment?
faqs.a: Your township or city assessor sets it. The county Equalization Department only tests that assessments across the county sit near 49 to 50 percent of value.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to take a residential assessment to the Tax Tribunal?
faqs.a: The petition is due July 31 of the tax year for residential property, after a protest to the board of review. Commercial and industrial petitions are due May 31, under MCL 205.735a.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate to record a Bay County deed?
faqs.a: For a warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed, yes. The certificate comes from the County Treasurer for $5 on a separate check, and quitclaim deeds without a warranty covenant are excluded under MCL 211.135.
